reply:
PostgreSQL treats NULLs as distinct from each other in UNIQUE constraints by default, so yes—you can insert multiple NULLs.

My first answer was too broad. SQL behavior on this varies by database. PostgreSQL's default is NULL ≠ NULL for constraint purposes. MySQL and most others follow the same pattern. Only with PostgreSQL 15+ `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` does a UNIQUE column reject duplicate NULLs.
